metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Vehicle locations extracted from traffic video frames and reformed as position matrices, used as high-dimensional inputs for the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: Wattleworth [10] firstly formulated a linear programming model to optimize a fixed signal timing plan for ramp metering based on historical traffic volume data.
nodes_source.description: Data used in a prior work [10] to optimize fixed signal timing plans for ramp metering.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Cited work only [10], no direct availability information in this paper.

nodes_source.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_source.description: Traffic measurements, specifically mean mainline occupancy during k-th and (k+1)-th cycles, used by the PI-ALINEA method for comparison.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Used for comparative method (PI-ALINEA) in simulation, no source or acquisition path stated for this specific data.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations and form position matrix
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw traffic video frames within a control area of size XxY. These locations are used to create a position matrix m_t at each time step t. The matrix also includes signal state information.

nodes_process.node_name: Stack and down-sample position matrices for state
nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st: St = {mt-(N-1),..., mt}.
nodes_process.description: To capture vehicle dynamics, position matrices m_t from N consecutive time steps are stacked to form the state s_t. For computational efficiency, this stacked representation is then down-sampled to reduce input dimensions while retaining vehicle position information.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward rt after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, > 0, w < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward r_t is defined to balance improving vehicle mobility and reducing vehicle delays. It is a linear combination of the average speed (v_t) in the merging area and the average queue length (q_t) at the on-ramp, with positive weight mu for speed and negative weight omega for queue length.

nodes_process.node_name: Approximate Q-function with deep neural network
nodes_process.source_quote: We adopt a deep neural network termed Q-network to approximate Q*(s, a). The neural network contains several convolutional layers and fully connected layers.
nodes_process.description: A deep neural network, referred to as Q-network, is used to approximate the optimal action-value function Q*(s,a). This network comprises several convolutional layers for feature extraction from video frames and fully connected layers to estimate the Q-value.

nodes_process.source_quote: The training problem can be viewed as the regression problem with the loss function defined by the following: L(w_i) = E_s,a((Q*(s,a) - Q(s,a,w_i))^2)
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using a multitask deep Q-learning approach. This involves minimizing a total loss function L(w_i) that combines L1 (for Q-value approximation) and L2 (for predicting mean speed and queue length simultaneously). The training process uses experience replay, a target network, and an epsilon-greedy strategy for action selection. Weights are updated using the Adam optimizer.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: The DRL method is evaluated using SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator. The simulation models a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, including a one-lane on-ramp, a three-lane mainline merging, and a gradual reduction to three lanes downstream. Speed limits are set for mainline and on-ramp. Driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: To accommodate the input size for ramp metering, the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture, based on Mnih et al. [30], is revised to accommodate the input size for ramp metering. It consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one fully connected (FC) layer per output layer. The total number of weights in the network is approximately 2 million.
tools_mentioned: Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] (version not stated)
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA method is implemented as a baseline. It fixes the green phase length and calculates the red phase length using a formula that depends on the previous red phase length and downstream occupancies (previous and current cycles) relative to a desired occupancy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of the DRL method against two baselines: no control and PI-ALINEA. Each scenario is run 20 times, initialized with different random seeds. The training phase involves 10^6 training frames.

nodes_process.source_quote: The results demonstrate that, in comparison with a state-of-the-practice method, the proposed DRL method results in (1) lower travel times in the mainline, (2) shorter vehicle queues at the on-ramp, and (3) higher traffic flows downstream of the merging area.
nodes_process.description: The performance of the DRL method is evaluated by comparing it against no-control and PI-ALINEA scenarios based on mean vehicle travel times in the mainline, queue lengths at the on-ramp, and traffic flows downstream of the merging area.

nodes_process.node_name: Conduct perturbation analysis of video data
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is conducted to assess how the DRL method's performance is affected by removing information from specific subareas of the control area. The control area is divided into eight subareas, and information from subarea 2 (where PI-ALINEA sensors are located) and other subareas is selectively removed for experiments.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate impact of perturbed data on travel time
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: The impact of perturbed video data on travel time is evaluated. Box plots of travel times are generated for simulations where information from different subareas is removed, and these are compared to a baseline using original data.
